newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium sends envoy to new Congo government.
newsitem.headline: Belgium sends envoy to new Congo government.

text.p: Belgium will send its special envoy for Africa's Great Lakes region to meet the new leaders in the Democratic Republic of Congo but will not resume cooperation unless certain conditions are met, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Thursday.

"Special envoy Yves Haesendonck will go to Kinshasa tomorrow to meet with the new authorities and possibly (self-proclaimed President Laurent) Kabila," Dehaene told a news conference after a cabinet meeting.
President Mobutu Sese Seko was ousted at the weekend by rebels led by Kabila who changed the name of Zaire, a former Belgian colony, as one of his first acts.
"We are ready to cooperate with the new regime, provided certain conditions are met," Dehaene said, reiterating a foreign ministry statement at the weekend.

"We want to see a broad-based new government which represents all Zaireans, we want to see the start of a democratic process with a view to elections, and we want international aid organisations to be given access to the (Rwandan Hutu) refugees," Dehaene added.
Dehaene declined to say what form a new Belgian cooperation could take.
Belgium cut its aid to the sprawling central African country in 1990, over charges that Zairean troops had killed students at Lubumbashi University who protested against the Mobutu regime.
